Shoprex

Turns an Android phone into a fast till and stock book for Tanzanian shops.

Overview

Most small shops run on a notebook. Shoprex puts selling and stock on the phone the shopkeeper already owns: scan a barcode, sell, and the stock and the day's takings update themselves. Owners get a web console to see every branch, worker and device. Swahili first, English ready, prices in TSh.

  • 3apps: API, owner console, Android
  • 1backend that owns every rule
  • 2languages, Swahili and English
  • 0database access from the apps

What it does

01Sell in seconds

Scan with the phone camera, adjust the quantity, take payment. Built for a queue at the counter.

02Stock that keeps itself

Every sale moves stock. Deliveries and corrections are recorded with who made them.

03Owners, managers, workers

Each role sees and does only what it should, on registered devices.

04Many shops, one owner

Branches, products and reports across the whole business in a web console.

05An audit trail

Every change to a price, stock or sale is kept, so mistakes can be traced and fixed.

06Swahili first

The whole interface reads naturally in Swahili, with English one tap away.

For the technical reader

How it's built

  • NestJS
  • Prisma
  • PostgreSQL
  • Next.js
  • React Native
  • Expo
  1. The NestJS API is the only service that touches the database. Web and mobile call it.
  2. Prisma and PostgreSQL. JWT auth with device registration and QR pairing.
  3. React Native with Expo: the camera for barcodes, secure storage for tokens.
  4. A Next.js owner console built on Radix UI.
  5. Built in phases, each closed by an acceptance check run end to end over HTTP.
